I'm a personal trainer at an all women gym.

Fat people tend to lie so much on their evaluations. They always think in their head they aren't actually as bad as they really are

Today I had a consultation with a female aged 25. So I meet this girl at the front desk, dressed in very expensive workout clothes, expensive shoes. She had a fit bit but it was almost covered by the fat around her wrist.

So went into my office and started out by asking questions about her life. I asked her how much resistance training she does a week. She does it six days a week. Then I asked about how much cardio. She runs every day. I asked her about eating habits. She says she only eats once a day, and it's always healthy like fruits, vegetables, whole grain rice, baked chicken. Never processed food or fast food. Drinks a lot of coffee and alcohol only on the weekends.

Did blood pressure, came back 167/120 or something like that. Pretty bad. She says it's because she drank two cups coffee this morning.

Put her on the scale. BMI of 44. Body fat percentage was way above normal. This is where she start to get upset. She immediately start talking about how she has water weight because of her menstrual cycle, and a lot of muscles in her legs weigh a lot because of running every day, her clothes add to it, she has much larger set bones. I showed her exactly how much of her body is fat, and how much is others (bones, organs, etc.) She told me the scale is not accurate and that her bones weight more than that.

The whole time she kept talking about how she is "a bit bigger" because of a thyroid issue she has had since grade school, and that all the scales and measurements and everything wasn't accurate for a person like her because she was healthier than most of her friends smaller than her.

So I put her to the test. We went out onto the floor. Started with simple squats. Bar with no weights.

Takes the bar, does a squat. Probably one of the worst squats I've ever seen. Her feet went out to the side, she bent her knees a little, and then she bent her upper body over. Then we tried it again. I told her to keep her back straight and to tighten her core. She went down, back bent again, and she put the bar down, pushing herself back up with her hands. Then she started getting mad at me, yelling about how she never does squats with a bar, and that she doesn't need to use the bar. So we went on to a different exercise.
